Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
Broken Card of the Week - 11/17/96

"There are some levels of power that no cost can justify."
- go...@best.com (Gomi no Sensei)

This week's card is one of the most unbalanced in the game,
and key to the deck that met The Corrupter's challenge to
break the Golden Tenets:

Return to Innocence 4 Blood Action
(D) Bleed your prey with +X bleed, where X is the capacity
of the acting vampire. Burn this vampire if the action is
successful.

This card is extreme, but is it broken? It can generate huge bleeds,
very easily -- a bleed of 15+ is not difficult to do with RtI, and
that's half of starting pool. It's possible to build up huge bleeds
in other ways, by using permanents, but those telegraph your punch.
It's also possible to do a few smaller bleeds in the same turn, for
the same total amount. But those require getting more than just
one bleed through.

Return to Innocence, in contrast, is a trump. You don't know it's
coming, and it is overpowering. It does not allow your defense to
gradually degrade -- everything is over, at once, and there you
are, waiting for the next game. You can either counter-trump it,
or you are lost.

There are only three defenses: another 'broken' card, Archon
Investigation; Deflection of some sort; heavy intercept (and
this will not work if the player is using unblockable bleed --
Day Operations, Horrific Countenance, Walk through Arcadia -- to
get the RtI through). Finally, it's not difficult to sidestep
the cost of the card, steep as it seems. In combination with
Possession, Malkavian Dementia, or a Soul Gem, it's almost free.
And anything that lets you see your opponent's hand will
eliminate the risks of Investigation or deflection.

There is one last problem: it's used to defend another card
which probably shouldn't be part of the set:
"But there's a defense against RtI! With Archon Investigation, it is not so
bad!" Return to Innocence and Archon Investigation are used to
justify each other, in a dance of circular reasoning. Archon
Investigation is the counter for Return to Innocence, while Return
to Innocence is used to justify the necessity of Archon Investigation.

How broken is RtI? (on a scale of 1-10)
Overall rating: 9.0
James Hamblin: 8.0
Peter D Bakija: 9.0 "Ban this sucker. It is just plain wrong."
Rulemonger: NR
Sean Whittaker: 10.0 "Ban the damn thing."
Steve Bucy: 9.0
Tom Doehne (yt) : 9.5

Can it be fixed? Not according to the raters, who give banning the
card a whoppingame more]

Here are the alternatives:
Do nothing: 0 (this got -1s).

This Action may not be modified: 1.0 The card becomes wallpaper.

No Bleed Enhancers can be played: 2.1 Just doesn't do enough to fix it.

Cost is 4 pool instead of 4 Blood: 5.6 Cost is more in line with benefit,
but it's still a trump.

And the favorite actual fix, at 7.0: (LSJ give this a 9)
Add/change the following text:
This vampire is removed from the game (not burned) if the action is
successful. If successful, the target Methuselah may burn one or more
vampires she controls to reduce the bleed by (1+X) for each vampire
burned, where X is the capacity of the burned vampire.

It's a fairly significant change, and banning it's probably simpler. A
ban also removes the excuse this card provides for tn.

Next week's card: Another (more obviously) trump card, Direct Intervention

Comments welcome.
--
Tom Doehne

Hello all.
I agree completely with this card being banned and I haven't
even seen it used in a game! It's just one of those cards
that (as you said above) one minute your playing and having
fun and the next your ousted. There are just too many things
wrong with it (like it's cost being no cost at all, either
you stop it or your dead.) to allow it to be an unbroken
card. Ban it's what I say. However, I believe that what you
said about Archon investigation is more questionable. I think
that having a card to make people think twice before a big
bleed is most definately not 'broken'. A game where everybody
blleds for huge amounts is a boring game. Most decks will not
be stuffed with archon investigations as they are useless
when playing in an experianced playing group (unless one of
them is gambling...) so I don't see what the problem is. If
this card was banned then non-deflectors are at such a
disadvantage when faced with a bleed deck they will not be
able to compete and therefore the only decks that will be
played will have bleed bounce capabilities which IMO is
taking variation out of the game. This card slows down
bleeders to a reasonable pace and therefore makes the game
more tactically challenging (I.E Not just bleed for as much
as they can but perhaps just limit themselves to three) and
gives well designed decks a universal tactic against heavy
bleeds. I cannot therefore see what the problem is, however I
have a feeling someone will 'enlighten' me.....

AI has three problems:
1) Cost is disproportionate to the effect
2) It doesn't stop S&B, but it kills Bruise & Bleed and Tap &
Bleed
3) It encourages the existence of other trump cards.

1). The cost of AI is disproportionate to the effect.
The effect of AI is to get back a large chunk of pool that you
just got bled for and unpreventably burn an opponent's (active) vampire.
For this you pay 3 pool.
Vulnerability is the only other Master card that burns a vampire,
and it costs 2 pool, can be countered by SR, and doesn't get you pool
either.

2). AI doesn't stop S&B, but it kills Bruise & Bleed and Tap & Bleed
As many people have pointed out, AI does not eliminate S&B from
the game. Presumably, if the Malks can get one bleed through at +3
stealth, they can get as many as they like. Instead of getting one bleed
through for 7 pool, they get 3 for 3. Entirely true.
Unfortunately, the B&B (Tremere, Brujah, Toreador, Giovanni) and
Tap&Bleed (Toreador, Ventrue, Brujah) clans can't guarantee that they'll
get one bleed through on any given turn. The few times they do get a
bleed through, the bleed has to be for as large as possible, or they'll
die (the race between B&B and S&B will almost always go to the S&B if the
bleeds are confined to 3 pts or less).
AI hoses these clans. I mean, do you block Anvil with a Laptop
and Legal Manipulations, thereby losing a vampire, or do you take the
bleed and AI, losing 3 pool and destroying Anvil? Gee, I just don't know.
(Hell, I'd usually pay 3 pool just to torpor Anvil, if such a card
existed).

3). It encourages the existence of other trump cards.
AI exists, so RtI is balanced. Ai needs to be toned done, so
Direct Intervention enters the card set. And so on.

Finally, as far as bleed defense goes:
Intercept, blood gain, rush, bounce, or race. Why is this a hard
concept?
Good intercept decks stop good stealth decks about 1/2 the time.
Blood gain decks can laugh off S&B ("Well, I lost 12 pool last turn, so
I'll have to call these to Consangineous Boons to get back 14, and then
take 5 blood off my blood dolls... no problem"). Rush decks- I've never
been in a game with Malks and a Rush deck where Ozmo wasn't burned at
least once. Usually twice (Malks brought him out again). Bounce is
self-evident. Race - ever see a Malk deck prey on another?
AI isn't needed, because well designed decks can deal with S&B
about as well as they can deal with anything else.

OK, AI hurts stealth/bleed. It hurts Malk decks a lot, actually. The
point of a Malk stealth/bleed deck, not surprisingly, is to bleed for
a lot. If you restrict Malks to bleeding for <=3 each time, that means
they have to live for longer, which is difficult since they have almost
no combat defense (except Obedience, but if you can only bleed for 3,
you'd need to tap out and not be able to play Obedience). There are
plenty of other good cards for stopping stealth bleed. Most of them
say something like "+x intercept", and Elder Intervention/Pack Tactics
don't even require a discipline.

It's called bruise and bleed for a reason (I like stating the obvious).
Sure it'll have some combat, but a B/B bleed will usually get destroyed
in combat by a pure combat deck, or do poorly against a S:CE deck. It's
difficult to build a deck that's great in combat and still have room left
for bleed mods. So, if you restrict the B/B decks to bleeding for 3 and
not the occasional bleed of 5 or more, they're hurt a lot also, and you
don't hear people complaining about overpowerful B/B decks too often,
except maybe Tremere. Also, you mention that mods would be used more
than actions. This might be true for the Tremere or Giovanni, but the
Brujah and Toreador have 1 bleed mod, and at least 7 presence bleed
actions, and the actions also have good side effects. So, a presence
bleed deck can't rely on Aire of Elation.

>As for Tap and bleed - a good player will probably be wary of a tap and
>bleed deck building up for a big bleed and so would let through a 3 bleed so
>that the Tap & Bleed deck can't majesty and bleed him for 7 instead. How

a laptop and bleed for 4, you should be prepared to block it, bounce
it, or take it. The methusealh controlling Anvil would equip him
with a laptop because a bleed of 4 hurts his prey more than a bleed of 3,
and thus his prey will either lose more blood or be more likely to block
and possibly lose a vampire. Bruise and bleed decks aren't that scary
if the max bleed is only 3.

>Thats a good point that I never thought of w.r.t the RtI line - AI does
>balance it. Perhaps RtI is not so broken anyway?

No, that's not a good point. Justifying one trump with another is a
really bad idea, as many other people have said.

>What does direct intervention do (never seen this card)?

It's a Sudden Reversal for minion cards that costs 1 pool.

>Fair enough. I never thought that intercept was not a good counter to bleed.

Yeah, who'd want to play NL, where lots of new and different strategies
are available, when we can all play CL and miss most of them? Wait,
maybe I *want* to see new ideas.

>Why does the fact that the card isn't needed make it broken? It makes the

Debating the merits and flaws of Archon Investigation from different sides
of the 4CL/NL fence is fairly pointless as the effect that AI has on a 4
Card Limit environment is vastly different that the effect AI has on a No
Card Limit enviornment (I have no wish to turn this thread into another
CL/NL debate. I am just pointing out obsefvable differences). In a 4CL
environment, AI is an important tool for keeping the balance because S+B
decks are completely unhindered by 4CL (due to the reundndancy of
Obfuscate and Dominate cards in the set), as opposed to all other deck
designs. Thus, under 4CL, S+B decks tend to either dominate the playing
field or are "shamed" out of the enviornment. Due to the design
restrictions caused by 4CL, there are no consistent bleed defenses:

Bleed Bounce is limited to 4 Deflections (excellent) and 4 of the new
Rederection (iffy), which kind of bite. If you are the Malkavians or the
Tremere, you can have 12, which is almost acceptable (because Redirection
and Telepathic Misdirection are of questionable reliability due to the
need for the superior ability) if you wish to have Bounce as a major
defense, but all single Dominate or Auspex clans are screwed as to bleed
bounce, especially considering how Redirection and Telepathic Misdirection
are only useful at superior.

Bleed reduction, which requires Telepathic Counter is no longer a viable
bleed defense when limited to 4.

Rush defense (i.e. Beat up the guy bleeding you before he kills you) is
more or less ineffective as a bleed defense under 4CL, as vastly discussed
under the "4CL and Rush" thread elswhere in this group.

Race defense (kill my prey before I am dead...) is the only really
reliable bleed defense under 4CL, which means to compete with a S+B deck
you need to play a S+B deck.

Under NL, all of these defenses are perfectly viable, and usually
perfectly effective. Under 4CL, AI is a needed defense against S+B, as
there are no other reliable defenses other than the threat of AI to slow
down the speed of S+B. Under NL, big S+B decks don't do all that well, as
decks than can generate big bleeds on a consistent basis just get eaten
alive by Rush decks ("Oh no! Ozmo has been burnt! Again!"). The biggest
problem I have found to deal with in NL are weenie S+B decks (like the
"Setite" deck posted by James Hamblin recently in another big thread),
where the vampires rarely ever bleed for more than 3, so AI is no help
anyway.

Under NL, Archon Investigation is completely unneeded, and verges on
complete overkill. Under 4CL, AI is a needed staple, if only to deal with
S+B decks.

You know, that's amazing. Most people, when told of a card
that is broken and another card which was made broken because of the
first card would assume that getting rid of both cards would be good
for the game. What you are doing here is wanting to keep AI so
badly that you would reconsider the merits of RTI.
Put it this way-suppose I have a heavy bleed deck. Suppose
all my friends play heavy bleed, and the only distinction between the
winner and the losers is who pulls out the RTI first. Suppose, also,
that all my friends have Archon Investigation, too. Yes, it is
balanced in this playcircle. But it is also skewed so badly that

that it is an unfair card. With fairness in mind, we allow AI to be
played with also because it is fair that both the bleed and anti-bleed
be played. So, with an eye to fairness, we play with unfair cards.

There are no merits to either RTI or AI, and there are none
for Direct Intervention, a Master OOTurn which costs 1 pool to cancel
a minion card played-burn the card played and return the blood to the

any intelligence at all to use.

First of all, I'll say that I agree with your AI stance. I think it adds
variety to the game.

I want to discourage people from banning malk decks though. Malk decks
can definitely be made as a pure sneak and bleed deck and those are nasty,
but not all malk decks are pure sneak and bleed. In my play group once
we find a deck combo that is devastating and can only be stopped by
specific types of decks we generally don't play them anymore. If you
don't think people in your group will agree to this then just make a deck
specifically designed to cream it. Just about any nasty deck you can
think of has a counter deck that can cream it rather easily. As an
example most people seem to think that S&B is the nastiest combo around
but if you make a good Brujah rush deck you can torpor their vamps the
same turn they come out and they'll never get ANY bleeds in. After a few
sessions like this most people will agree to play a more imaginative and
fun deck.

I will qualify this by noting that certain cards like thoughts betrayed
are completely broken and virtually unbeatable decks can be made with
these. If people insisted on playing a deck like this I would just refuse
to play with them.

If you play tournaments and are just trying to come up with killer combos
then feel free to disregard everything I've just said because you won't
end up with killer decks this way. What you will end up with are decks
ranging from interesting to really bizare that are really fun to play.
You will also end up with longer games that really give you time to
develop odd strategies. I'm not saying once you've made a deck you can't
play it again, just ditch the really nasty ones so people have a chance to
try something interesting.

standards of the original set), so I'm not very upset to see them
smashed. Perhaps Computer Hacking would have been a better example of a
card IC members dare not play.
I am still slightly annoyed by the unimaginative & unsubltle way WotC
chose to handle the problem that existed in the original "Jyhad" set (where
Malkavians & other bleeders dominated). The other new anti-bleed cards
of the V:tES ed., such as Elder Intervention and Protected Resources,
might have been an adequate fix on their own, together with the modified
rules on Ag damage which enhanced combat aspect of the game.
Also, they could have been more imaginative in finding solutions.
In the old set, Malkavian Dementia was a great card for keeping the Malks
in line, besides which it emphasized the storytelling aspects of the game,
by reminding us that the Malks are insane. A few more
such cards emphasizing the weaknesses of clans that were dominant,
would, IMO, have been more fun than cards which work to deprive them of
their strengths. AI adds nothing to game atmosphere.
Also, what AI discourages most is 4 bleeds, rather than higher
ones. After I first came aware of AI, the first thing I did was develop
a deck of massive hi-powered bleeders (my "Queen Anne" deck), on the
idea that, if I was going to risk AI I might as well make the most of
it. This deck was able to inflict bleeds of 10 (without RtI). One the other
hand, I would be very reluctant to put together a deck in which Ozmo
might bleed with conditioning.
I'm also annoyed by the way AI hampers my efforts to develop a
deck of effective Nosferatu stealth bleeders. (I like Nosferatu, despite
their weaknesses & constantly try to find ways to make them effective).
Spying Mission is one of the few bleed enhancers available to them, but
is rarely used by Malks, who have far more effective bleed strategies.
But even though Spying Mission is definitely NOT a powerful card it is very
difficult to use effectively without bleeding for more than 3. Suppose
Agrippina Night Moves you twice, modifyies each with Spying Mission, and
then burns them both on a successful Computer Hacking for a total bleed
of 6. This is not excessive. Agrippina had to work hard for this 6
bleed, taking 3 actions. This averages only 2 bleed per action, which is
no higher than 3 Computer Hackings. Its advantages (which I won't go into
unless someone's interested) are barely justified by the fact that this
strategy requires superior Obf. It seems hardly fair that Agrippina is
thereby at risk of being instantly burned. Worst of all, your prey knows
the big bleed is coming, and so decides not to discard the AI in his
hand.
Anyway, sorry for the long and rambling post. I hope not too far
off the original subject (Direct Intervention & Return to Innocence, I
think--I say ban the suckers! RtI is way too powerful. DI, whether too
powerful or not, simply causes things not to happen, thereby adding
nothing to the game atmosphere & making for boring play).

Messages.Body:
Nathan Harada (i...@hula.net) wrote:
: Direct Intervention under 4CL is even worse.

Everything is worse under 4CL. Let's argue about Direct Intervention insofar
as it affects Jyhad the way it was meant to be played.

: I hate Counterspell. I hate it. I don't like Power Sink and

: Spell Blast either, though those are both better than Counterspell.

Magic: The Gathering is a different game. Though designed by the same
person, it operates under very different conditions. A basic requirement
which M:tG has (which Jyhad thankfully doesn't have) is speed of development.
Countermagic as a strategy is balanced by its lack of speed: if you're going
to play countermagic, you're not playing cards which can damage your
opponent. And in M:tG you must meld (play cards which aid your position)
quickly, or you're dead. In Jyhad, you meld at much the same rate as your
opponents: there are fewer means of accelerating your position, and most of
them hurt you if you try to go too fast.

Now to trumps, the real object of this discussion. First off, what's wrong
with the very concept of a trump? Nathan Harada proposes banning Sudden
Reversal and Merrill Molitor:

: Hey, guys! Let's ban Sudden Reversal-yes, I really mean it. Why

: shouldn't the SR trump go, too? Is it only because it was in the
: basic set, along with Merill Molitor, that we aren't including it

: in this trump-hating session? Why is this trump fairer than the
: others?

I'm supposing by responding to this paragraph that it isn't mere hyperbole,
though it sure sounds like it. Merrill Molitor is hardly a trump: if he's a
trump, then every card in the game that prevents aggravated damage is by
definition a trump and worthy of banning. Skin of Night ought to be considered
more of a trump than Merrill, who can only transform one lousy point of
aggravated damage. Merrill _may_ be undercosted; that's a different issue.
He's certainly not as flagrantly undercosted as Antoinette DuChamp, whom I've
complained about in another posting (because unlike every other Caitiff, she
has an inferior discipline, Presence, without an accompanying drawback. Why's
that?)

So let's proceed to talking about trumps. Let's define trumps carefully
first. Trumps are _NOT_ just cards which can be immediately played to negate
the effect of other cards; my Skin of Rock is not a "trump" because it made
your Lucky Blow ineffective. Rather, trumps are cards which actively change
the playing environment because they require their inclusion in any
competitive deck.

By this definition, Tomb of Rameses III is not a trump, but a somewhat
undercosted card. Sudden Reversal is similarly not unbalanced: it does unto
you exactly what it did to the other guy (costing you a card and a master
phase). Thus can we please focus just on the effect on deck composition that
Return to Innocence and Archon Investigation have had, and not on their
relationship to one another? If you can produce a serious argument that
no deck can ever stand a chance at competition without one or both of these
cards (as little chance, say, as a top-of-the-line Type II deck stands against
a top-of-the-line Type I deck, since you favor M:tG analogies), then I'll
agree they're worthy of banning. But I've yet to be convinced that intercept
and rush strategies can't keep these cards in line.

- Neil

1) Doesn't burn the bleeder. Sends the bleeder to Torpor.

Rush: eliminate their vampires
Bleed Bounce: send their vampires downstream
Intercept: stop their actions and kill them
Blood Gain: Get so much blood that their bleeds are meaningless
Race: Oust my prey before my predator ousts me

Heavy bleed does have a way of dominating the game; not to the extent of
always winning, but to the extent of requiring every deck to pack very
heavy bleed defense. But better than an all-or-nothing card like AI would
be a rules change such as "no more than one action or action modifier can
add to a given bleed action". This would stop those weenies from popping
